investigation.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocks All Agent Provisioning Evals (production-api)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-31T03:56Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm gateway ELB endpoint in us-east-2 was unreachable during agent provisioning. Because the failure occurs at the POST /api/agents call before any agent identity or VM state is returned, zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were collected, causing a complete contract gap for all three checks.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — the AWS ELB in us-east-2 that backs the /v1/agents provisioning path — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api layer returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" on every POST /api/agents attempt, preventing agent creation from starting and making it impossible for the eval runner to collect any required evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure connectivity failure localized to the swarm gateway dependency; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact beyond the observability eval is unconfirmed.

investigations.title: model-matrix eval failure: aura-gpt-5-5 returns 502/424 provider_account_unavailable
investigations.summary: The model-matrix eval failed because exactly one of two configured models, aura-gpt-5-5, returned a 502 bad-gateway wrapping a 424 Failed Dependency with error code provider_account_unavailable. The other model, aura-claude-sonnet-4-6, passed cleanly. This is a localized eval failure scoped to the aura-gpt-5-5 model route; no sibling checks failed and no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The AURA runtime harness successfully reached the POST /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test endpoint for aura-gpt-5-5 but the upstream model provider was unreachable at the time of the eval run (2026-08-31T03:55:51Z). The provider layer returned HTTP 424 Failed Dependency with code provider_account_unavailable and the message "AURA is temporarily unable to reach the model provider. This is an issue on our side, not with your account or credits." The harness surfaced this as a 502 bad_gateway to the eval runner, causing the model result to record ok=false, provider=null, and resolvedModel=null. Because the contract asserts allPassed=true and failedModelCount=0, the single model failure was sufficient to fail the entire check.

The production-api layer returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" on every POST /api/agents attempt, preventing agent creation from starting and making it impossible for the eval runner to collect any required evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure connectivity failure localized to the swarm gateway dependency; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact beyond the observability eval is unconfirmed.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Agent Provisioning Evals (production-api)
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-31T03:56Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm gateway ELB endpoint was unreachable during agent provisioning. Because the failure occurs at the POST /api/agents step — before any agent identity, model, or runtime evidence can be collected — every required evidence field (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) is absent and the expected-output contract is fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting /v1/agents) was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning" on every POST /api/agents call. Because agent creation is the first step in all three remote-agents checks, none of them could proceed past provisioning, producing a uniform failure with zero evidence collected. This is an eval-observed infrastructure availability issue localized to the swarm gateway dependency; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to production end-users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.
